requirements.evidence: All contract classes are present: CreateQueue (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:15) trims the name, checks it is 1-255 chars, uses Str::slug($slug ?? $name), checks for a duplicate within the entity and converts a QueryException to a ValidationException. UpdateQueue takes named nullable params and excludes its own slug with whereKeyNot (app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:38-43). SetQueueAccess upserts or revokes, and only logs a revoke when $deleted > 0 (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:35-45). The QueuePolicy has create/update/manageAccess/call, and call denies on corrupted values. The queue_access migration has cascading FKs and the unique pair. The ordering in Ticket::call() is right: lock, inactive check, Gate authorize, then LogicException (app/Models/Ticket.php:96-109). CallNextTicket authorizes after the active check. The docs and CHANGELOG are updated. One weakness: isUniqueViolation treats any SQLSTATE 23000, which covers FK and NOT NULL failures too, as a duplicate slug. The policy also relies on User::membershipFor, which is not shown in the diff.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through app/Actions and authorize inside via Gate::forUser(...)->authorize. The policy is the single source of truth and the old inline membership check was removed from Ticket::call. The model declares #[Fillable([...])], matching the sibling style. Docs are synced in business-rules.md, database-schema.md and CHANGELOG. Deviation: the migration name 2026_10_29_000001_create_queue_access_table.php has a hand-picked timestamp rather than one produced by make:migration, though down() is reversible.

security.evidence: Every action authorizes first (CreateQueue.php:17, UpdateQueue.php:16, SetQueueAccess.php:18). Both call paths enforce the 'call' ability (CallNextTicket.php:32, Ticket.php:105). Permissions are validated as known strings (SetQueueAccess.php:25-30), and cross-entity membership/queue pairs are rejected. Corrupted permissions deny instead of granting. Mass assignment is restricted with #[Fillable]. There is no UI surface.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/QueueManagementTest.php covers: create/slug defaults, invalid names, per-entity uniqueness, unauthorized create/update with no writes, update combinations, own-slug vs taken slug, deactivation blocking issue and call, a policy matrix, corrupted permissions, audit logging via a mocked channel (including no log on an empty revoke), invalid/cross-entity/self-grant cases, unauthorized calls in every mode, a granted employee calling, authorization before the waiting check, and the factory and enum. Existing CallNextTicket tests were adjusted only by adding owner memberships, not weakened. Gaps: no test simulates the race-time QueryException-to-ValidationException conversion; no test for an employee without a grant (only outsiders) in CallNextTicket; no test that Ticket::call checks for an inactive queue before authorization when called by an unauthorized user.

simplicity.evidence: isUniqueViolation is copy-pasted between CreateQueue.php:52-62 and UpdateQueue.php:70-80, and so is the slug-length/duplicate validation. QueuePolicy::call (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php ~455-480) decodes the raw JSON by hand with nested if/elseif branches where a short is_array check would do. Owner/admin role checks are repeated in call() and isManager().

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods focused, and the PHPDoc on Ticket::call and the policy methods is updated. The defensive decoding branch in QueuePolicy::call is verbose. There is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: actions, enum, model, factory, migration, policy, both call paths, docs and tests. There is no delete action and no UI. The CallNextTicketTest edits are needed because the new authorization would otherwise break existing tests.

issues.explanation: isUniqueViolation returns true for any SQLSTATE 23000, which also covers foreign-key and NOT NULL violations, so unrelated integrity errors are reported as a 'slug already in use' ValidationException.
The unique-violation helper and slug validation logic are duplicated across both actions instead of being shared.
No test exercises the race path where the DB unique index fires and must become a ValidationException, a requirement stated explicitly in the task.
The unauthorized CallNextTicket test uses only a non-member outsider; there is no test for an entity employee without a grant, or with a grant on a different queue.
The migration's hand-picked timestamp suggests it was not created with php artisan make:migration, as the conventions require.
The hand-written JSON decoding with nested branches in call() is more complex than the corrupted-value requirement needs.
definition() eagerly creates an Entity even when the caller overrides both foreign keys, leaving orphan entities behind.

review.summary: The change adds CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess actions, the queue_access table, model, factory and enum, and a QueuePolicy that is enforced in both CallNextTicket and Ticket::call() in the required order, with docs and thorough feature tests. Authorization and validation are sound and the scope is tight. The remaining problems are duplicated, over-broad unique-violation detection, an untested race-conversion path and some verbose policy code, so it is approvable with minor follow-ups.
